*   Reconstruct and store the low-resolution data block for these nodes [S1][S2].

The claim states that the evidence supports the action to 'Reconstruct and store the low-resolution data block for these nodes [S1][S2].' Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly describe the 'EVERY-K storage strategy,' which involves reconstructing and storing low-resolution data blocks for nodes at every k levels starting from the root. These nodes are defined as 'representative nodes.' Since the claim refers to the nodes described in the evidence (S1 and S2) and the action described in the claim is exactly what is detailed in the provided text for those specific nodes, the evidence fully supports the claim.

*   Because units with similar errors are in the same bucket, and they are distributed round-robin, neighboring units with similar errors are assigned to different processors [S1][S2].

The evidence in both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly states that the algorithm uses 'error-guided bucketization' where distribution units are sorted into buckets based on their error ranges (implying units with similar errors are in the same bucket). It further states that these units are distributed among processors in a 'round-robin manner'. Finally, both sources conclude that this specific combination of mechanisms ensures that 'neighboring distribution units with similar errors will be distributed to different processors'.
